A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, New Bounds for Sparse Variational Gaussian Processes. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching the earlier experimental Appendix C to Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 and Appendix C report original Gaussian and Poisson regression experiments, including predictive scores, optimization curves and comparisons with exact or full GP models.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds learned-parameter diagnostics in Figures 2 and 4 and Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 newly sketches a multi-function non-Gaussian adaptation using a separate covariance-scale parameter v per GP function. This extension is not evaluated. The core regression objectives and prediction procedure remain unchanged; the explicit minibatch equation documents the existing stochastic method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Snelson, Pol, Bike, Elevators, the same eight large-scale regression datasets, synthetic Poisson data and NYBikes. The new diagnostics use retained datasets. Multiclass models are discussed prospectively, without new evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: Exact GP, SGPR and SGPR-artemev for medium-scale regression; SVGP, ODVGP and SOLVE-GP for large-scale regression; and Full GP and SVGP for Poisson regression. The newly cited Bui et al. (2025) work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Reported splits, kernels, inducing-point budgets, preprocessing, optimization settings and predictive metrics remain unchanged. The added parameter histograms use existing runs. Replacing the Figure 5 panel does not establish a changed protocol: both versions specify the same M=8,16,32 Poisson settings.

E4.justification: Figures 2 and 4 add distributions of learned variational parameters for Pol, Bike and Elevators at both inducing-point budgets. Table 3 and Appendix D.3 add fitted-hyperparameter and Poisson-scale diagnostics, extending analysis of how the approximation behaves within existing experiments.

E5.justification: The five random-split repetitions and standard-error reporting are retained. The new histograms describe variational parameters from one existing run, rather than introducing uncertainty estimation across runs. No additional seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds fitted Snelson hyperparameters and reports Poisson v values around 0.675 for synthetic data and below 0.01 for NYBikes. Figure 5 replaces the M=32 panel that duplicated Figure 3's M=16 plot in v1. All retained predictive-score tables, including their standard errors, are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds omitted outer logarithms to two expressions in the Bayesian GP-LVM bound derivation. Remark 3.4 also adds the matrix inequality V* <= I and its covariance implication. The principal bounds, lemmas and supporting proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims: relaxing the conditional-prior assumption yields tighter scalable bounds, supports stochastic and non-Gaussian extensions, and can reduce underfitting and improve predictions. The additional diagnostics support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 explains covariance shrinkage and explicitly notes that the tractable predictive distribution has higher variances than the expensive alternative. It connects the Elevators parameters near one to small covariance residuals and explicitly states that non-Gaussian experiments cover only single-function models.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 now explicitly gives the N/|B| minibatch scaling and identifies the precise regularization-term replacement needed in existing implementations. These clarify implementation of the retained method; initialization, optimizer, hardware and data-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction newly acknowledges concurrent Bui et al. (2025) work using the same conditional variational family and similar objectives. V2 also adds references to Leibfried et al. (2022), Damianou et al. (2016), and Lazaro-Gredilla and Figueiras-Vidal (2009), while retaining the broader related-work discussion.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized explanatory and spelling edits, adds acknowledgements and an impact statement, and replaces the review notice with publication information. A new hyperparameter Appendix C shifts the existing experimental appendix to D; the main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 gain third rows of histograms, Table 3 is added, and Figure 5's right panel is replaced. Captions and float placement are adjusted, with existing tables renumbered or relocated. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves accuracy through the logarithm corrections in Appendix B.5 and replacement of the duplicated Figure 5 panel. Parameter diagnostics, clearer implementation instructions and concurrent-work attribution also improve transparency. These are useful but limited gains: the core approach, empirical coverage and predictive-score evidence remain largely unchanged.
